why_flagged: A user submission claimed release_year 2025 and factory HATSA (Honduras) for Johnny Tobacconaut. Independent research shows a more complex history: the name dates to 2015 (an entirely different Nicaraguan-puro blend made in Honduras under Davidoff distribution), went on hiatus, returned in 2021 as a Luxury Cigar Club exclusive, and was reformulated into the current Connecticut Shade/Mexican/Nicaraguan blend as a core-line relaunch in 2023 after STG's 2022 acquisition — now made at Tabacalera A.J. Fernandez in Esteli, NICARAGUA, not HATSA. The submission's 2025 date actually belongs to a separate, limited-run "10th Anniversary" edition (itself a different Nicaraguan puro blend, badly affected by a factory fire that destroyed over half that release) which the submission itself correctly flagged as a distinct product. Set release_year to 2023 and factory to A.J. Fernandez/Nicaragua instead of the submitted values.
proposed_action: No action needed — this entry documents why the submitted release_year/factory were corrected rather than used as-is.

item: Aladino Cameroon — submission contained a FABRICATED award and multiple wrong facts
why_flagged: This submission's headline claim — a No. 2 Cigar of the Year (96 points) from Cigar Aficionado's 2022 Top 25 — is FALSE. Directly fetched the actual 2022 Top 25 list: Aladino Cameroon does not appear on it anywhere. The real #2 for 2022 was Rocky Patel Sixty Sixty; #1 was H. Upmann No. 2. No Aladino product of any kind appears on that list. This was not used. Additional errors: release_year was submitted as 2021, but the line actually launched May 2020 (confirmed via halfwheel/Cigar Coop coverage). The wrapper was described as "authentic African Cameroon wrapper tobacco" grown in Cameroon, but it is actually Honduran-GROWN Cameroon-SEED tobacco from the Eiroa family's own Jamastran Valley farms — never grown in Cameroon itself. Factory was given as "Fabricas Unidas"; the more specific and commonly-cited name is "Fabrica de Puros Aladino," a converted vintage movie theater (Fabricas Unidas appears to be a related/parent entity). Vitola names and dimensions were also substantially wrong: "Petit Corona" (4.5x46) does not match the real "Elegante" (4.5x48); "Toro" (6x52) should be named "Super Toro"; "Lonsdale" was submitted at 6.5x44 but is actually 6x43; a "Corona" at 5.6x44 does not match any known Aladino Cameroon vitola at all and was not added. The submission also omitted 3 real vitolas (Lancero, Gordo, Queens Perfecto).
proposed_action: Treat this submission's source as unreliable going forward — this is the first submission this session with a wholly fabricated award citation rather than a research/attribution error. Flagged directly to the site owner.
